source.title: Compositionality and Ambiguity: Latent Co-occurrence and Interpretable Subspaces

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE-latent co-occurrence and interpretability in language models, a different method from the original toy-model work, and reports results relevant to whether dictionary features serve as model representation units.
record.gate_note: The study also reports SAE-width and L0 trends, plus qualitative cluster case studies. It cites toy-model and other SAE results from prior work; those cited findings are not recorded as rows. The study does not test whether extra toy-model features are dropped, nor whether LLM activations are one feature per neuron or orthogonal direction.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether SAE latents in GPT2-Small and Gemma-2-2b fire independently, by comparing observed co-occurrence with the independence expectation. It also shows cases where a latent's role is clear only inside its cluster. These results bear on whether dictionary latents are self-contained units of the model's representation (V5). The study takes SAE feature recovery (V4) as given rather than testing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add that SAE latents are not independent, that clusters map interpretable but often non-linear subspaces, and that the phenomenon appears confined mainly to small SAEs with coarse-grained latents. They also note that some latents can only be understood through their co-occurrence relations.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes activations from pretrained language models using SAE-latent co-occurrence graphs, Jaccard similarity, clustering, and PCA; it does not train toy networks to test superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE width changes co-occurrence and cluster size; L0 changes cluster size and the apparent compositionality of the qualitative-amount cluster. The study also uses different SAE architectures for GPT2-Small and Gemma-2-2b.

fits_no_version.finding: Co-activation of latents for different word senses on ambiguous tokens, proposed as a readout of model uncertainty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latent co-occurrence reflects ambiguity between word meanings.

fits_no_version.finding: Clusters map ring-shaped or non-linear subspaces, such as concentric day-of-week rings split by a leading space; irreducibility is not tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-dimensional feature subspaces appear as co-occurring SAE latent clusters.

record.problems: Many width and co-occurrence results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The case studies are qualitative and explicitly non-exhaustive; the clustering depends on a threshold chosen to limit the largest subgraph to 200 nodes. The study does not establish causal function, and some interpretations are presented as possibilities requiring further work.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for additional qualitative clusters listed only in the appendix or explorer, since the post describes them as a non-exhaustive set and does not give separate outcome detail for each. Other plotted trends on active-latent fraction and sparsity are not direct measures of the versions' feature-unit claims.

untested.parts: There is no test of capacity competition or of how polysemanticity relates to feature importance.
There is no test of polysemantic neurons; the study's ambiguity and composition findings concern SAE latents, not neurons.
The study assumes SAEs recover interpretable features. It does not measure how features are distributed across neurons, nor how well SAEs recover features.
Stability across training runs and completeness are not tested. Only independence of firing and context-dependence of interpretation are examined.
Ring-shaped and multi-latent subspaces are described from PCA of latent activations, but irreducibility is not tested.

missing.what: Gemma-2-2b mean subgraph size decreases as L0 decreases, with matching subgraph sparsity across L0.
Ordinal-word cluster: latents that look redundant individually separate by relative strength in cluster context.
Gemma clusters are in general less interpretable than GPT2-Small clusters, and the most active latents in a subspace are less often cluster members.
missing.locator: Future Work, Alternate LM and SAE architectures

missing.what: Month cluster lacks a spoke for May although a May latent exists; that latent is isolated.

record.verdict_notes: LessWrong post, not peer reviewed. Evidence is qualitative case studies from a non-exhaustive search plus figure-only trends with no numbers in the text. The clustering threshold is chosen to cap the largest subgraph at 200 nodes. Different SAE architectures are used for the two models: ReLU for GPT2-Small and JumpReLU for Gemma-2-2b.

versions.untested_parts: No small toy networks are trained or tested for superposition, feature dropping, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of whether neuron polysemanticity results from limited capacity, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study discusses ambiguity and composition in SAE latents, but does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
It studies SAE latents in GPT2-Small and Gemma-2-2b, but does not test how features are distributed across neurons or establish comprehensive recovery of the underlying model's features.
It evaluates interpretability and co-occurrence, but does not test feature stability across runs or settings, completeness, or whether SAE latents are canonical units of the model.
It describes multi-latent clusters and subspaces, but does not test whether underlying superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE-latent co-occurrence against the expected rate under independence across SAE widths.
rows.measure: Observed latent co-occurrence per token versus expected co-occurrence under independence
rows.baseline: Expected rate if latents were independent, E[co-occurrences(i,j)] = p(i) * p(j)
rows.value: The observed distribution is broader than the independence expectation: many latents co-occur less often and some more often than expected; co-occurrence rate and prevalence of above-expectation cases decrease as SAE width increases.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and distribution but gives no numerical values for the plotted results.
rows.check: Co-occurrence measures independence of SAE latents, not whether models spread features across neurons, so V4 is removed. Against V5 the state is partial, not observed: most latents are independent, but a subset co-occur above chance and this shrinks with width. No numbers are given (figure only).

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. The observed co-occurrence distribution is broader than the independence expectation; this does not establish dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality.
source_check.locator_found: Methods, Measuring SAE latent co-occurrence; Results, Figures 7–8; Appendix Figure 2.
source_check.problem: Statistical independence is treated as a measure of V5's stronger claim about representational units.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE-latent co-occurrence against the expected rate under independence across SAE widths.
rows.measure: Observed latent co-occurrence per token versus expected co-occurrence under independence
rows.baseline: Expected rate if latents were independent, E[co-occurrences(i,j)] = p(i) * p(j)
rows.value: The text reports that co-occurrence decreases monotonically as SAE size increases, with some latents co-occurring more frequently than expected; above-expectation cases become less prevalent at larger widths.
rows.note: The text describes the trend but gives no numerical values for the plotted results.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: V4 removed. Gemma-2-2b layer 12 shows the same pattern, with above-expectation co-occurrence declining with width. Special tokens were excluded; figure only.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Co-occurrence decreases with width, and above-expectation co-occurrences become less prevalent; completeness, stability and canonicality are not measured.
source_check.locator_found: Methods, special-token exclusion; Results, discussion of Figures 7–8; Appendix Figure 3.
source_check.problem: The co-occurrence trend cannot establish partial satisfaction of V5.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured co-occurrence-cluster subgraph size across SAE widths.

conditions.value: different widths; individual values not stated for this result

rows.measure: Mean subgraph size, including and excluding isolated latents
rows.value: Subgraph size decreases as SAE width increases; the decrease is clearest for subgraphs larger than one node.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the trend but gives no plotted numerical values.
rows.check: V4 removed. Cluster size falls with width, so how far latents act as independent units depends on the chosen SAE width. The clustering threshold was chosen so the largest subgraph has at most 200 nodes.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Mean cluster size decreases with SAE width, especially when isolated latents are excluded; individual feature identity across widths is not compared.
source_check.locator_found: Results, SAE co-occurrence clusters are smaller and fewer in large SAEs; Figure 9; Appendix Figure 5.
source_check.problem: Changing graph cluster size does not measure stability or canonicality of dictionary units.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured co-occurrence-cluster subgraph size across SAE widths.

conditions.value: Gemma-2-2b SAE layers; individual layers for this width result not stated

rows.value: The appendix reports subgraph-size results across widths; the main text states that cluster size decreases as SAE size increases.
rows.note: The figure is described, but no numerical values or layer-specific trend are stated in the text.
rows.check: V4 removed. The Gemma width trend appears only in Appendix Fig 5; layers are not specified.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Appendix Figure 5 reports Gemma-2-2b cluster-size comparisons across widths without numerical values or feature-identity comparisons.
source_check.locator_found: Results, SAE co-occurrence clusters are smaller and fewer in large SAEs; Appendix Figure 5, right panel.
source_check.problem: Cluster-size variation is insufficient to determine whether dictionary features are complete, stable or canonical.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Compared co-occurrence-cluster size and composition in SAEs with different L0 sparsity.
rows.measure: Cluster size and apparent compositionality for the qualitative-amount cluster
rows.value: At L0 22, a similar five-node cluster appears to form more distinct categories and to show less compositional encoding.
rows.locator: Results, discussion of Figure 11 and layer-12 lower-L0 cluster 111; Appendix Figures 4 and 6
rows.note: This is a qualitative comparison; the text also says the effects of SAE sparsity on co-occurrence need further exploration.
rows.check: V4 removed. This is a qualitative comparison of one cluster: at L0 22 the categories look more distinct and less compositional than at the canonical L0 of 80.47. The quantitative L0 trend in Appendix Fig 6 is not captured by this row.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. The layer-12 16K SAE with mean L0 22 has a similar five-node cluster with apparently more distinct categories than the canonical SAE with mean L0 80.47.
source_check.locator_found: Results, paragraph after Figure 14; Future Work, Effect of SAE Sparsity on co-occurrence.
source_check.problem: A qualitative difference in compositionality across L0 settings does not measure feature completeness, stability or canonicality.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Examined a four-latent co-occurrence cluster and the PCA of its SAE-latent activations.
rows.measure: Interpretation of latent combinations for qualitative quantities expressed with “of”
rows.baseline: Individual latent interpretations: “one of,” “one of n,” “some of,” and “all of”
rows.value: The hub latent activates across cases, while spoke-latent combinations correspond to groups such as “each of” and “most of”; relative strengths of “some of” and “all of” latents track a continuum from “many of” to “almost all of.”
rows.note: The authors present this as a qualitative case study of compositionally interpretable SAE latents.
rows.check: V4 removed. Meanings are encoded by combinations and relative strengths of latents, so single latents are not complete units. The authors add that the composition is predictable from the latents read alone. Baseline is the individual latent interpretations.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Examined a co-occurrence cluster and PCA of its SAE-latent activations for days of the week.
rows.measure: Latent interpretations and activation patterns across token forms
rows.baseline: Individual spoke latents denote days of the week
rows.value: The spoke latents remain independently interpretable as days; the hub latent combines with them to distinguish tokens without a leading space, a role not apparent from examining the hub alone.
rows.note: The example includes both independently interpretable latents and a hub whose function is clearer in the cluster context.
rows.check: V4 removed. The spoke latents are independently interpretable, but the hub latent's role (no leading space) is not apparent from examining it alone.

source_check.locator_found: Results, Figures 17–21, especially the discussion following Figure 21.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Examined a five-latent co-occurrence cluster and PCA of activations on URL-subdirectory tokens.
rows.measure: Whether latent combinations correspond to token position within a URL subdirectory
rows.value: The PCA separates single-character token cases by distance into the subdirectory, and cluster latents activate at different sections; the authors say the composition may recover position but that its accuracy needs confirmation.
rows.note: The authors explicitly qualify the interpretation and say further work is needed to establish positional accuracy.
rows.check: V4 removed. The compositional reading of position is tentative; the authors say a larger SAE might give one latent per position.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Positional encoding by latent combinations is tentative; positional accuracy is left for future work, and composition in the underlying LM is explicitly unresolved.
source_check.locator_found: Results, Figures 15–16; Future Work, Understanding the drivers of co-occurrence and Accuracy of compositional encoding.
source_check.problem: Tentative positional composition does not establish incomplete or noncanonical dictionary units.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Examined co-occurring SAE latents for grammatical uses of “how” and activation along a PCA continuum.
rows.measure: Latent activation and interpretation across uses of “how”
rows.baseline: Latents at the PCA extremes associated with distinct uses, including degree, manner, and question uses
rows.value: Latents are generally independently interpretable at the extremes; examples between extremes activate multiple latents, which the authors suggest may reflect ambiguity. The exclamative use is not observed in this cluster.
rows.note: The interpretation that mixed activations represent uncertainty is proposed, not established by a direct uncertainty measure.
rows.check: V4 removed. Latents are interpretable at the PCA extremes and co-activate in ambiguous cases; the link to uncertainty is proposed, not measured.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Latents remain generally independently interpretable, and intermediate examples activate multiple latents; uncertainty is a proposed interpretation.
source_check.locator_found: Results, Distinguishing between uses of the word 'how'; Figures 25–27; Appendix Figures 20–24.
source_check.problem: Coactivation during ambiguous usage does not itself show that dictionary units are incomplete, unstable or noncanonical.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Examined a five-latent co-occurrence cluster and PCA of activations for apostrophe-marked possessors.
rows.measure: Latent activation across types of possessor
rows.baseline: Latents at PCA extrema associated with inanimate objects, specific people or groups, and generic people
rows.value: The cluster separates these possessor categories; between extrema, the primary latent for one category decreases while another increases, which the authors interpret as co-occurrence in ambiguous cases.
rows.check: V4 removed. Qualitative ambiguity case, same pattern as r9.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Possessor categories occupy PCA extrema, with changing relative latent activation between them; the ambiguity explanation is qualitative.
source_check.locator_found: Results, Distinguishing the type of entity whose possession is indicated by an apostrophe; Figures 28–30; Appendix Figures 25–26.
source_check.problem: The ambiguity case does not measure completeness, stability or canonicality of dictionary features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Examined a co-occurrence cluster and compared its latents with a linear-probe direction for number words.
rows.measure: Cluster coverage and latent similarity to the number-word probe direction
rows.baseline: The set of latents with high cosine similarity to the probe direction
rows.value: The cluster activates for number words from “two” to “ten,” but not “one”; some latents similar to the probe direction, including the latent maximally activated by “one,” do not co-occur strongly with the clustered latents.
rows.note: The authors suggest feature absorption may be relevant but state that the cause is unclear.
rows.check: V4 removed. The latent for 'one' is missing from the cluster despite high similarity to the probe direction, possibly from feature absorption. The authors cannot tell whether this is a property of the SAE or of the model.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. The latent for 'one' exists in the dictionary but does not join this co-occurrence cluster despite high similarity to the probe direction; absorption is suggested, not established.
source_check.locator_found: Results, Encoding of continuous properties in feature strength without compositionality; Figures 22–24; Appendix Figures 18–19.
source_check.problem: Missing membership in a co-occurrence cluster is not missing coverage by the dictionary.

source_check.notes: The cited synthesis sentence accurately describes this study; its other numerical results concern other studies. Trends are qualitative or figure-only; underlying-model composition, uncertainty, and absorption explanations remain tentative.

reader_labels.reason: The study reports interpretable SAE-latent clusters and examples of compositional or ambiguity-related structure in both models (r6–r11), alongside measured co-occurrence and width trends (r1–r5).
